# Identity test fixtures

<!-- Generated by scripts/record_identity_observations.py from tests/data/identity/observed.json (real somalier output). Do not edit by hand. -->

The sample identity checks (ID001-ID005) are tested against real `.somalier` files for the Genome in a Bottle Ashkenazim trio. This trio comprises HG002 (son), HG003 (father), and HG004 (mother). The files are in `tests/data/identity/` (about 210 KB each). The values below were reported by somalier 0.3.5 for these files. They are generated, not entered by hand.

## How the fixtures were made

- The 17,766 common hg38 sites bundled with somalier are committed here as `sites.hg38.vcf.gz` (somalier is provided under the MIT licence).
- For autosomes, the Genome in a Bottle v4.2.1 GRCh38 benchmark genotypes are used for each individual. A site absent from a benchmark VCF is treated as homozygous for the reference allele (hom-ref) in that individual, because the VCF lists variants only. Hom-ref calls outside the benchmark's confident regions are therefore an assumption.
- For chrX and chrY, genotypes were called with `bcftools mpileup | bcftools call` from the public Illumina NovaSeq 35x BAMs (GRCh38, no-alt analysis set) at the 365 chrX and 17 chrY sites. The benchmark VCFs do not include chrX, so these calls are what make sex checking possible.
- The genotypes for each individual were processed as a single-sample VCF with `somalier extract`. The procedure is documented in `scripts/fixture_recipe/`.
- Direct extraction from the BAMs was not used, because streaming a 46 GB BAM took hours per sample and used several GB of memory. Since the inputs come from VCF, the files contain genotypes only and no read depth. somalier therefore does not infer sex itself, and ngs-preflight instead uses the proportion of heterozygous chrX calls (see ID004).

## What somalier reports

Relatedness over 17,766 sites (the permitted parent-child range for ID002 is 0.35-0.65):

| Pair | Relatedness | IBS0 | IBS2 | Sites compared |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HG002 / HG003 | 0.501 | 23 | 10593 | 17,384 |
| HG002 / HG004 | 0.495 | 32 | 10560 | 17,384 |
| HG003 / HG004 | 0.009 | 1397 | 8015 | 17,384 |

Per sample (sex is inferred by the tool from chrX heterozygosity. HG002 and HG003 are male, and HG004 is female):

| Sample | Sex | Hom-ref | Het | Hom-alt | Unknown | chrX het | chrX hom-alt |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| HG002 | male | 6,866 | 6,871 | 3,647 | 0 | 1 | 134 |
| HG003 | male | 6,895 | 6,863 | 3,626 | 0 | 0 | 129 |
| HG004 | female | 6,908 | 6,821 | 3,655 | 0 | 117 | 72 |

## Engineered failures

For each row, the identity checks were run on the trio with 1 deliberate mistake. Findings are counts per check.

| Scenario | Mistake | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| `trio` | nothing, the true family | none |
| `duplicate` | HG002 submitted a second time as HG002_copy | ID001 x1 |
| `swapped` | HG002 (son) and HG003 (father) swapped in the pedigree | ID002 x1 |
| `wrong_sex` | HG002 declared female in the sheet | ID004 x1 |
